To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pilin and sortase residues critical for EbpA, B, and C incorporation into Ebp pilus fibers have been defined, and that SrtA is required for EbpB processing and pilus cell wall anchoring.
pilus subunit organization and compartmentalization in Enterococcus is unique and is dependent on the sortase recognition sequence and pilin motif of each subunit.

the Lys residue in the pilin-like domain of EbpC is critical for Ebp pilus fiber polymerization, while only the sortase recognition sequence of EbpA and only the pilin-like sequence of EbpB are required for their incorporation into the pilus structure.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EbpC pilus subunit is required for pilus assembly and is essential for the incorporation of EbpC into the Ebp pilus fiber.
the EbpA pilus tip subunits are incorporated into the Ebp pilus fiber through their sortase recognition motifs, while EbpC base subunits are incorporated through their pilin-like motifs.
pilus biogenesis is an extremely complex and highly regulated mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pilus-associated pilin and sortase residues critical for Ebp pilus assembly in Enterococcus have been identified and defined.

we have identified the residues within the EbpC pilin that are required for pilus fiber polymerization, we have defined the minimal pilin-like motifs required for incorporation of each Ebp pilin subunit, we have shown that the EbpB pilin is processed and cell wall anchored by the housekeeping sortases, and we have identified the EbpB SrtA Cys residue that is required for EbpB cell wall anchoring.
we have defined molecular mechanisms of Ebp pilus polymerization and subunit organization in Enterococcus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pilin-like motifs of the pilin and minor pilins are critical for incorporation of pilin subunits into pilus fibers.
the molecular mechanisms governing pilus biogenesis can vary among different pilus systems and even between different pilus subunits within the same system.
the pilus tip and base subunits are incorporated into the pilus polymer by different mechanisms, and this may have implications for pilus assembly in other bacteria.
